# Operator Guide (`docs/handover/operator-guide.md`)

**Current cut — [follow-up 20](follow-up-20.md) (2026-10-31 EDT):** #341 generates authenticated reporting; #342 retains pending receipts when result_url is missing; #344 permits verified same-boot restart adoption under the original lease. D-133 and open acceptance rows remain explicit.
Previous cut: [follow-up 19](follow-up-19.md), through #337.

## Reporting and restart changes at #344

Installer 7 requires `--control-url` as a validated HTTPS origin and a readable
`--server-ca`. It generates `result_url` at
`POST /api/v1/agent/update-results`, server trust from that enrollment CA, and
the enrolled node's mTLS certificate/key paths. `allowed_artifact_origins` is
exactly the control origin. Invalid inputs fail before host changes. A
same-release rerun repairs reporting fields/server CA and preserves identity,
usage, updater journal and unrelated settings. `install --allow-loopback` is
an explicit **TEST ONLY** opt-in for an isolated HTTPS lab, false in production.
The distinct artifact-origin question remains with updates 11; no additional
origin is authorized by this handover. See [installer configuration](../node/install.md#authenticated-updater-reporting-f10-02-136-13103).

If sealing logs `result_url_missing`, the receipt remains **pending**, with its
original bytes and no ACK. Explicit `Engine.Flush` without a sink returns
`VALIDATION_FAILED`; local apply success is not central delivery. Repair the
reporting configuration, then run `fvpn-updater flush --config /etc/vpn-node/updater.json`
to transmit the identical pending receipt once. Verify the central ACK; do not
rebuild the receipt or rerun the update to manufacture a new result.
[Updater 18 evidence](follow-up-20.md#installer-7-and-updater-18--341--342).

After a short agent process restart on the same OS boot, a still-valid original
signed lease can retain serving without a new control response, intermediate
baseline or Apply. Adoption requires matching desired/applied generation,
the original clock anchor, a fresh serving heartbeat, eligible release,
fresh DNS/probe checks, full kernel/topology verification, healthy meter
ownership and clear identity/updater barriers. Operators can see retained then
adopted serving under the **same absolute deadline**. Ordinary stop checkpoints
the last usage delta and leaves its epoch open; updater withdrawal still
finalizes it. Failed qualification closes forwarding while keeping control
access; OS reboot or a lost anchor cannot adopt the old lease. Same-generation
repair queues the failed verifier report before repairing with the original
lease; recovery does not erase that observation. Retain agent/watchdog reason
logs and all baseline/heartbeat producer rows for isolation 10. This contract
does not identify ISO-F6-03's historical writer or establish zero pre-D loss.
[Agent 28 evidence and D-133](follow-up-20.md#agent-core-28--344-historical-writer-still-unattributed).
